## Detection

- `GET_HWINFO` (command `$28`) device 0 returns the product string (device: `C64 Ultimate`); device 1 returns a count then 5 bytes per decoder: UltiSID 1, UltiSID 2, then each enabled socket. Entry: address low, address high, `$00`, `$00`, type (source: 2, or 3 when the mask is not `$FE` (split or mirrored), for UltiSIDs; 4 or 5 for sockets; `+128` is set on every entry. bytes 3-4 are `$00` in the public source: the dual-chip second-address case never triggers, do not rely on them). A socket is listed only if `SID Socket 1/2` (store `SID Sockets Configuration`) is `Enabled`. Device: 10-SID map gives `04 00D4.. 20D4.. 40D4.. 60D4..`. Parts, second SIDs and the chip type are not listed. REST `SID Sockets Configuration` gives `SID Detected Socket 1/2` (None, 6581, 8580, ARMSID, ARM2SID, FPGASID, SwinSID Ultimate, PDsid, SIDKick ...) for a host installer.
- ENV3 test (device: 10 windows by 10, both from the 6510 and by REST, gives the identity matrix): silence all; at window i set voice 3 to triangle or saw at a high frequency, attack 0, sustain 15, gate on, volume 15; wait two frames; read `$1C` of every mapped window: window i gives `$FF`, all others `$00`. Close the gate afterwards. Do not use OSC3 `$1B` (keeps changing). Any other window that also reads `$FF` means an overlap: fall back to a smaller map.
- Test only mapped windows. Without UCI (no `$C9`), play one SID at `$D400`.
- Device: REST `writemem` to the Socket 1 window was sometimes also heard on Socket 2 (6510 writes were clean): check both sockets' ENV3 before REST sound tests.

## Differences in sound

- UltiSID: filter curve per UltiSID (`8580 Lo`, `8580 Hi`, `6581`, `6581 Alt`, `U2 Low`, `U2 Mid`, `U2 High`), `Filter Resonance` `Low`/`High`, `Combined Waveforms` `6581`/`8580`, `Digis Level` (`Off`, `Low`, `Medium`, `High`), set in store `UltiSID Configuration`; both UltiSIDs can differ. Defaults: curve `8580 Lo`, `Filter Resonance` `Low`, `Combined Waveforms` `6581`, `Digis Level` `Medium`. Use single waveforms and curve-tolerant filters.
- Sockets hold chips with their own filter, DC and noise; the two ARMSID differed ten times in volume click and two times in triangle level (device).
- A `$D418` volume step clicks: 900 (UltiSID) to 1400 (ARMSID) of 32767 per step; 0 to 15 is 0.4 to 0.6 of full scale (device). Step by one at most, only on silent chips.
- Same-frequency unison: two UltiSID parts add to 0.71 of the sum; UltiSID against ARMSID gave 0.32 (triangle), 0.74 (saw), 0.99 (pulse) (device). Do not rely on unison for level; detune slightly. The same 440 Hz on four chips panned apart gave a moving, spacious beating field by ear (device): stereo movement without modulation.
- Socket chips are written over the 1 MHz cartridge-side bus (c64://ultimate/hardware).

# REU (RAM Expansion Unit) on Ultimate Devices

**Summary:** Ultimate devices emulate a 1750-compatible REU (128 KB to 16 MB) in SDRAM, registers at `$DF00-$DF0A`. DMA stalls the CPU, REU contents survive C64 resets, and the REU is disabled by default. No REST endpoint writes REU memory: data gets in through boot-time preload, UCI LOAD_REU from game code (DOS `21`, or Control `04 08` for the configured preload image), or a stash stub. Games use it for level data, charset/sprite/bitmap streaming and sample storage.
**Read when:** storing or streaming game data via the REU, writing DMA routines, or deciding how to load an REU image.

Sources: REU gateware `fpga/cart_slot/vhdl_source/reu.vhd` and firmware of GideonZ/1541ultimate master 700c7f2fa (2026-11-13); the U64-family top level that instantiates `reu.vhd` is not public. "Measured" = benchmark of 2026-11-13 on Ultimate 64 Elite firmware 3.15a and C64 Ultimate firmware 1.2.1 (c64://ultimate/bench), or "measured U64" = Ultimate 64 Elite, firmware 3.15a, 2026-11-20. Related: c64://ultimate/uci (LOAD_REU commands), c64://ultimate/hardware (turbo, `$DE00-$DFFF` map), c64://memory/map, c64://io/spec.

records.name: data/ultimate/reu.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/ultimate/reu.md#Timing, stall, size, wrap -->
- The CPU is halted for the whole transfer (no wait loop needed; the status is valid on the next instruction). A raster/CIA IRQ falling inside it fires late. Menu freeze pauses a running transfer.
- Measured 2026-11-13 on Ultimate 64 Elite fw 3.15a and C64U fw 1.2.1, PAL, 16 MB REU; rerun: c64://ultimate/hardware#rerun or c64://ultimate/bench. The rate depends on the CPU turbo setting (1 byte per microsecond holds only at 1-3 MHz). Bytes per microsecond, stash / fetch, screen blanked: 1 MHz 0.99 / 0.99, 2 MHz 1.97 / 1.97, 3 MHz 2.96 / 2.93. Top speed: U64 48 MHz 5.1 / 3.6, C64U 64 MHz 7.8 / 4.3. Not monotonic: U64 4 MHz fetch 2.0 and 6 MHz stash 3.0; C64U 10 MHz stash 4.9 against 7.7 at 8 MHz. Floors from 6 MHz up: U64 3.0 / 2.6, C64U 4.9 / 2.9.
- With the screen on and badlines the measured rate is 5 % lower; none with `$D031` bit 7 set. Each transfer has a fixed overhead of 3 to 15 PHI2 ticks (1-byte transfers: 15 at 1 MHz, 3 at top speed).
- At 64 MHz an unrolled `sta abs` fill (4 cycles per byte at 63 CPU cycles per microsecond) stores 15.75 bytes per microsecond, twice the REU stash rate of 7.8: fill memory with the CPU at top speed.
- **512 KB wrap:** without the extended registers the REU address bits 23-19 stay at the value written to `$DF06` for the whole transfer while bits 18-0 count (`reu.vhd:137-140`), so a transfer that crosses a 512 KB boundary (`$080000` multiple) wraps inside that block. VICE does the same. Rule: split every DMA so `(addr & $07FFFF) + len <= $080000`; length 0 means 64 KB. Extended builds count all 24 bits and mask them to the configured size.

records.name: data/ultimate/reu.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/ultimate/reu.md#Timing, stall, size, wrap -->
- **Size detection** (no UCI command reports it): fetch the byte at REU offset 0, stash back `a^$A5`, fetch again (no REU if it does not hold; restore it). Then for s = 64 KB, 128 KB, ... 8 MB: save bytes at 0 and s, write `a^$A5` at 0 and `a^$5A` at s; if offset 0 now holds the second value the REU aliases at s, so size = s. Restore the bytes. No wrap up to 8 MB means 16 MB. Also verify a magic header and block checksums after loading: a missing or stale REU returns valid-looking stale data without error.
- **`$FF00` trigger** (b4 = 0): set the command, change `$01` (e.g. to `$34` for RAM under I/O), then store to `$FF00`. With `$01` = `$34` the trigger fetched 256 bytes into RAM under I/O (measured on Ultimate 64 Elite, firmware 3.15a, 2026-11-20). A CPU copy of `$D000-$D0FF`, taken with `$01` = `$34`, matched the stashed bytes; the last byte was `$00` because the test had cleared that source byte before the stash. The VIC registers `$D000-$D02E` kept their values except the raster, light pen and collision registers, which the VIC updates itself. A bounce buffer in normal RAM, copied with the CPU, does not depend on the trigger. DMA writes to colour RAM (`$D800`) need I/O mapped in.

records.name: data/ultimate/reu.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/ultimate/reu.md#Timing, stall, size, wrap -->
- Turbo: the REU gateware of 2026-08-28 (`g_no_dma_delay`, "no initial delay on U64/U64E2, because of Turbo Mode", commit 59594060b) stops the CPU in the cycle of the `$DF01` write; the earlier gateware inserted one cycle in which the CPU ran on at turbo speed. Rule for every core: disable interrupts from the first register write to the trigger, follow `sta $DF01` with `nop nop`, and put no instruction there that depends on the transfer. Core 1.50 contains this change (measured on Ultimate 64 Elite, firmware 3.15a, 2026-11-20): with `U64 Turbo Registers` and CPU Speed 48, a 1-byte fetch followed directly by `lda $C000 / sta $C001` left `$C001` different from `$C000` in 0 of 3000 runs (3 runs of 1000).

records.text:
<!-- Source: data/ultimate/reu.md#Pitfalls (most often violated) -->
## Pitfalls (most often violated)

1. REU is disabled by default; a stale or absent REU returns valid-looking data: check presence, magic, checksum at boot.
2. `$DF01` is the last register write; no compiler reordering; clear `$DF0A` fix bits after use.
3. Split DMAs at 512 KB boundaries; length 0 means 64 KB; autoload restores base values (use no-autoload for consecutive blocks).
4. Reading `$DF00` clears flags and IRQ; `$FF00` mode leaves a pending command until `$FF00` is written.
5. VICE charges DMA at 1 cycle per byte (VICE 3.10, measured) and an image must equal the configured size; test streaming budgets on hardware.
6. `RAM Expansion Unit` = `GeoRAM Mode` replaces the REU: a 256-byte window at `$DE00-$DEFF`; writes to even addresses in `$DF80-$DFFE` select the 256-byte page inside a 16 KB block (bits 5-0), writes to odd addresses `$DF81-$DFFF` select the 16 KB block (bits 7-6 of the even register extend the block number past 4 MB); both are masked to `REU Size` (`fpga/cart_slot/vhdl_source/all_carts_v5.vhd:644-653`).

# Ultimate Command Interface (UCI)

**Summary:** UCI is a polled register interface at `$DF1C-$DF1F` (`$DF1B` = IEC device number; a loaded EasyFlash `.crt` moves it to `$DE1C-$DE1F`) through which a C64 program asks the Ultimate to read/write files, open sockets, make HTTP requests, load files straight into RAM or REU, change the palette and reboot. It is off by default. Commands are `<target> <command> <args>`; replies are data bytes plus a status string. Targets: 1/2 DOS, 3 Network, 4 Control, 5 SoftwareIEC, 6 HTTP.
**Read when:** a game must load levels or data from the Ultimate's storage, save high scores, change the palette, use the network, or detect an Ultimate.

Sources: firmware `software/io/command_interface/`, `software/filemanager/dos.cc`, `software/io/network/network_target.cc` and the gateware `fpga/io/command_interface/vhdl_source/command_protocol.vhd` of GideonZ/1541ultimate master 700c7f2fa (2026-11-13). "Measured U64" = Ultimate 64 Elite, firmware 3.15a, 2026-11-20; "measured C64U" = C64 Ultimate, firmware 1.2.1, 2026-11-13. "Since YYYY-MM-DD" = commit date in the public master; a device can run older firmware. No UCI version command exists: send the command and check for `21,UNKNOWN COMMAND`. Docs: https://1541u-documentation.readthedocs.io/en/latest/uci/index.html. SDK (MIT): https://github.com/barryw/ultimate-uci-sdk. Enable with `c64_config` ("C64 and Cartridge Settings" / `Command Interface` = Enabled).

<!-- Source: data/ultimate/uci.md#Exchange -->
- The firmware sets no timeout that the C64 can see. Bound every poll loop with a deadline from the jiffy clock (`$A0-$A2`, advanced 60 times per second by the KERNAL IRQ from CIA 1, which keeps C64 time under turbo); network and HTTP commands wait for the remote side.
- One command in flight; an IRQ handler may run but must not use UCI. During SoftwareIEC loads, REU DMA and U64_SAVEMEM the machine is halted (music and raster IRQs stop).
- A C64 reset aborts the command in flight, closes all network sockets and frees all HTTP header and body handles (`command_intf.cc:46-53,185-190`, `http_target.cc:1140-1143`). The DOS targets keep their open file and current directory. At startup send DOS CLOSE_FILE (`84` = nothing open is fine).

## Status strings

| Form | Used by | Success |
|---|---|---|
| `NN,TEXT` | DOS, Network, Control; SoftwareIEC OPEN, CLOSE, CHKOUT | `00,OK`; DOS READ_DATA blocks, FREEZE and REBOOT send no status bytes |
| `NNN TEXT` | HTTP target errors | `000 OK`; after an exchange: server response line plus headers (up to 255 bytes) |
| 1 binary byte (LOAD_EX: 3 bytes) | SoftwareIEC LOAD, SAVE, CHKIN, partition commands | `$00` |
| bare text (`DISK IS FULL`, `WRITE PROTECTED`, ...) | DOS filesystem failures | non-digit first char = failure |

Codes mean different things per target, so key on target plus code. `21` UNKNOWN COMMAND on every target.

| Target | Codes |
|---|---|
| DOS | `01` dir empty, `02` request truncated, `81` NOT IN DATA MODE, `82` file not found, `83` no such directory, `84` no file to close, `85` no file open, `86` can't read directory, `87` internal error, `88` no information, `89` not a disk image, `90` drive not present, `91` incompatible image, `98` function prohibited, `99` not implemented |
| Network | `01` connection closed by host, `02,NO DATA: <errno>`, `03` more data not supported, `04,DATAGRAM TRUNCATED: <n>`, `11,ERROR ON CONNECT: <errno>`, `12,SEND ERROR` / `ERROR ON CLOSE`, `81` invalid params, `82` parameter out of range (READ_SOCKET length above 1472), `83` interface not available, `84` unresolved host, `85` error opening socket, `86` internal error |
| Control | `81` invalid params, `82` errors on track, `83` not in data mode, `84` REU not enabled, `85` REU file cannot be opened, `86` REU offset > size (not saved), `87,DISK ERR: ...` (U64_SAVEMEM), `88` cannot open config file, `89` config file had errors |

<!-- Source: data/ultimate/uci.md#Target 4: Control -->
Not available: reset without reboot, run PRG, change CPU speed, single config get/set, SID/mixer control except by LOAD_CONFIG, input injection, power off. READ_RTC `02` answers `21`.

**Palette `$51-$54`** (U64 family only, `#ifdef U64` in `control_target.cc:250-301`; U2 family answers `21`; public master since 2026-09-03; a wrong length gives `81,INVALID PARAMS`): 8 bits per channel, applied to the whole display at once, kept in RAM only (nothing is saved). `04 53` and `04 54` measured U64. One blocking palette command took 12-58 ms on the measured C64U, so a program issues it as a non-blocking step (push the command, check the status once per frame, one command in flight) or under a fade, and never per raster line. Send `04 54` on exit. Raw: `04 53 02 FF FF FF` sets colour 2 to white. See also c64://ultimate/upic.

records.text:
<!-- Source: data/ultimate/uci.md#Target 4: Control -->
**LOAD_CONFIG** (`04 50 <name>`, default `/temp/uci_config.cfg`; `control_target.cc:559-609`, parser `software/userinterface/configio.cc:230-434`) is the only way a C64 program changes settings. Write the `.cfg` with the DOS target, then send the command.
- Format: `[Store Name]` line, then `Item=value` lines; lines starting with `#` or `;` are comments; at most 319 characters per line, item names at most 40. Only the listed items change. Enum values compare case-insensitively with spaces before and after ignored; string values are taken exactly; number items are read with `%d`. Stores: `[C64 and Cartridge Settings]` (`Command Interface`, REU items), `[U64 Specific Settings]` (`Turbo Control`, `CPU Speed`, `Badline Timing`, `System Mode`, `Palette Definition`), `[Audio Mixer]`, `[SID Addressing]`. A `.cfg` saved from the menu is a correct template.
- Status `00,OK`: every line applied and the changed stores effectuated. An unknown `[store]` or item is skipped, logged and still gives `00`.
- Status `89,CONFIG FILE HAD ERRORS` when any line has an invalid enum value, a non-number for a number item, no `=`, an empty item name, more than 319 characters, or stands outside a store section. Then no store is effectuated: the values of the valid lines are stored in RAM and take effect at the next apply of their store (a later successful LOAD_CONFIG or a menu change). Measured U64: one invalid line returned `89` with reply `Line 3: Value 'BOGUS' is not a valid choice for item Vol Drive 2`, and REST showed the valid line's new value. Fix the file and send it again. Turbo example: `CPU Speed=64` is invalid on a U64 / Elite MK1 and `CPU Speed=5` on an Elite II / C64U (c64://ultimate/hardware).

- Status `88,CANNOT OPEN CONFIG FILE` when the file is missing (measured U64) or when the name is not terminated by `$00`.
- Reply data = the parse log, at most 511 bytes.
- The file-browser load and the `run_prg` sidecar `.cfg` apply the valid lines even when other lines fail (c64://gamedev/toolchain).
- Changes stay in RAM: lost at power-off unless saved from the menu or with REST `configs:save_to_flash`. Example and SID use: c64://ultimate/multisid.

# Upic: 384x256 16-Colour Graphics by Border Racing

**Summary:** Upic is a software technique by Aleksi Eeben, not a hardware mode and not a register. With the VIC display disabled (`$D011` bit 4 = 0) the whole screen is border, and the CPU, running at Ultimate turbo speed, stores a colour to `$D020` once per pixel, cycle-exact against the raster beam. Result: 384x256, 16 colours (from the runtime palette), no colour clash, no hardware sprites, no text. It needs an Ultimate 64 / Elite / Elite II / C64U at top turbo speed, PAL. At 64 MHz game code gets 16.5 % (256 rows) to 26.7 % (224 rows) of the CPU cycles of a frame (measured C64U).
**Read when:** a request mentions Upic, a full-screen 16-colour bitmap without attribute clash on an Ultimate, or a game that scrolls and animates by palette cycling.

Sources: the public implementations below (renderer, file format, layout); turbo and palette rules from c64://ultimate/hardware and c64://ultimate/uci (GideonZ/1541ultimate master 700c7f2fa). "Measured C64U" = C64 Ultimate, firmware 1.2.1, PAL, 2026-11-13; "measured U64" = Ultimate 64 Elite, firmware 3.15a. Credit: Upic by Aleksi Eeben (https://csdb.dk/release/?id=263889). Public implementations: https://github.com/xahmol/mandelbrot-upic (Xander Mol, Christian Gleissner; Oscar64, GPL-3.0) and https://github.com/xahmol/ultimate-uci-oscar64 (library with Upic renderer, GPL-3: read for reference, do not paste its code into other-licensed projects). Cross-references: c64://ultimate/hardware (turbo), c64://ultimate/uci (palette commands), c64://ultimate/reu (REU data), c64://graphics/vic/spec.

<!-- Source: data/ultimate/upic.md#Requirements -->
## Requirements

| Need | Detail |
|---|---|
| Machine | Ultimate 64, Elite (48 MHz), Elite II, C64U (64 MHz). Not U2 cartridges, not a stock C64, not VICE (logic and buffers can be tested in VICE; the picture cannot). |
| Video | PAL (the renderer timing assumes 63 cycles per line and 312 lines) |
| Turbo | `Turbo Control` = the registers mode (`U64 Turbo Registers` on U64, `C64U Turbo Registers` on C64U, measured) and `CPU Speed` = top entry (`48` or `64`); the program then writes `$D031` = `$8F` (index 15). Index 15 is 64 MHz on the C64U (measured on C64 Ultimate, firmware 1.2.1, 2026-11-20), so a program that must run at 48 MHz there writes `$8E` (index 14: probe 201, 48 MHz measured); on U64 index 15 is 48 MHz. Set them with `c64_config` or with a `.cfg` named like the PRG (same folder, started from the Ultimate file browser; c64://gamedev/toolchain). Write exactly one `Turbo Control` line: a value the firmware does not list makes UCI LOAD_CONFIG answer `89` and apply nothing (rule in c64://ultimate/hardware). |
| UCI | `Command Interface` = Enabled, for palette commands (c64://ultimate/uci) |
| Firmware | palette commands `04 51`-`04 54`: U64 family, public master since 2026-09-03; present on the measured C64U (1.2.1). `21,UNKNOWN COMMAND` means they are missing. |

- Index 15 gives 48 MHz or 64 MHz depending on model; the register cannot tell. Probe (c64://ultimate/hardware).
- After a start the CPU runs at 1 MHz whatever `$D031` holds: 2.6 s after `run_prg` program start, 3.9 s after `load_prg` and a typed `SYS` (`upload_run_asm`), 4.17 s after a reset (measured on U64 3.15a) (measured on C64 Ultimate, firmware 1.2.1, 2026-11-20). Probe until two loop results agree before the first frame.

records.text:
<!-- Source: data/ultimate/upic.md#Renderer and CPU budget -->
## Renderer and CPU budget

- Per picture line: wait for the raster line, resync turbo by writing `$D031` = `$80` then `$8F` (so the CPU resumes at the same sub-slot on every line), then call a generated, page-aligned routine: patch-list loads, a delay loop, then per byte column: load byte, store to `$D020` (low nybble), table lookup `nyb[i] = i >> 4`, store to `$D020` (high nybble). End with two NOPs (without them pixel 383 is lost) and `$D020` = 0.
- 64 MHz: 63 CPU cycles per phi2 (VIC takes one of 64 sub-slots), 3,969 per PAL line; two pixels per 16 cycles, 16 pixels in 126 cycles; all 384 pixels one dot wide.
- 48 MHz: 47 cycles per phi2, 2,961 per line; free CPU time 0.75 of the 64 MHz figure (2,961 against 3,969 cycles per PAL line, screen blanked, measured 2026-11-13). The mandelbrot-upic picture is shown at 48 MHz (measured on Ultimate 64 Elite, firmware 3.15a, 2026-11-20). The number of pixels shown per line at 48 MHz is in Not verified.
- Never use indexed stores to I/O in the renderer (extra dummy read changes timing); a VIC register read costs one extra sub-slot, a write none.
- Free CPU cycles per 64 MHz frame (1,238,387 cycles), measured C64U (50 samples, status marker row on); at 256 rows the renderer takes 83.5 % of the frame:

| Visible rows | Free cycles / frame |
|---|---|
| 256 | 204,800 |
| 240 | 268,300 |
| 224 | 331,000 |

- Frame rate is the display refresh (50 Hz) as long as per-frame work fits the free time. If it overruns, raster lines shift and rows glitch; polled loops that call "show frame" between work chunks show the picture only on some frames (flicker). Interrupt-driven display (a raster IRQ that starts before the first displayed row, a hook at the end of the frame) keeps it steady.
- Each row not shown returns one raster line, 3,969 cycles at 64 MHz (the table: 16 rows = 63,500 cycles).
- Per-frame cost of a ring-buffer scroller at 64 MHz (cycle count of the code): one new column 3.8k cycles (scrolling left 4.2k), one new row 51k, diagonal 53k.
- A full-screen clear is 49,152 stores: 196,608 cycles with unrolled `sta abs` (4 cycles) and 245,760 with `sta abs,y` (5 cycles), the whole free time of a 256-row frame. Do not clear the screen per frame.

<!-- Source: data/ultimate/upic.md#What is impossible -->
## What is impossible

- Hardware sprites (invisible while DEN = 0, tested on hardware), text mode, bitmap/multicolour modes, colour RAM, raster bars by IRQ, any second raster interrupt, stable KERNAL IRQ chain. Anything that moves must be drawn into the buffer by software.
- Per-line palette tricks (UCI is far too slow). VICE preview of the picture.
- Interrupts and stalls inside the picture: CIA timer IRQs must be off; KERNAL/BASIC IRQ handlers must be bypassed (own vectors with ROMs out, `$01 = $35`; NMI to an RTI). **Host-side REST access (`c64_memory` read, screen capture) stalls the CPU** through DMA: in a measurement, 29 REST reads over 1500 frames produced 19 glitched frames, none without. Avoid it while Upic runs.

records.name: data/ultimate/upic.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/ultimate/upic.md#Game architecture on Upic -->
5. **Palette animation.** Reserve palette slots by role (ink, rotating water shimmer, sky, accent...) and animate by rewriting RGB, no pixel redraw: day/night keyframes, shimmer, flash. Never signal gameplay state by colour alone.
6. **Non-blocking palette writes.** A blocking UCI palette write took 12-58 ms (one colour) and up to 51 ms (all 16) on the measured C64U, up to 3 frames. Use a small state machine: queue one command, advance it once per frame (2k cycles per step in the budget above), at most one command in flight, timeout in frames, prefer one-slot updates. Never wait on UCI inside the displayed part of a frame; use absolute addressing for UCI registers. Measured C64U: 199 palette updates over 500 frames took at most 3 frames each, with no glitched frame.
7. **REU-fed data.** Map chunks, tiles, pictures, overlays and level data live in the REU and are fetched into hidden columns in the free time (c64://ultimate/reu). One 256-byte fetch per frame ran 500 frames without glitches (measured C64U). A 49,152-byte fetch stalls the CPU for 11.4 ms at 64 MHz (4.3 B/us) and 13.7 ms at 48 MHz (3.6 B/us), over half a 20 ms frame, and 49.6 ms at 1 MHz (0.99 B/us): only under a fade or in the free part of the frame.
8. **Overlays.** With the resident layout above, put code in REU overlays copied through a bounce buffer into a RAM window (including RAM under I/O run with `$01 = $34`); verify checksums on load; overlays call resident services rather than each other.
9. **Audio.** Compose the SID register image in the main loop, copy it in the frame IRQ hook (very short). Digis and CIA-driven music are not compatible with the display IRQ. Several SIDs: `c64://ultimate/multisid` (one register image per window).

<!-- Source: data/ultimate/upic.md#Detection and fallback -->
## Detection and fallback

- Run all checks on the normal text screen BEFORE setting DEN = 0 and print a plain message naming the setting to change: Command Interface off (`$DF1D & $7F != $49`), turbo registers missing (`$D031 = $FF`: `Turbo Control` is `Off` or `Manual`), speed not 64 MHz (the 48 MHz pixel count is in Not verified), palette commands missing (GET_PALETTE `04 51` answers `21,UNKNOWN COMMAND` on a U2-family cartridge or firmware without them), REU too small (size probe in c64://ultimate/reu).
- Speed probe and model: c64://ultimate/hardware. The speed probe, not the product string, decides 48 versus 64 MHz.
- No graphical fallback exists in the libraries: without turbo the renderer produces garbage. Offer a normal VIC mode path or refuse to start.
- Exit: undo every change the program made: stop the raster IRQ, set DEN = 1 in `$D011`, write `$D031` = 0, restore `$01`, the vectors and `$D020`, and send `04 54` to reset the palette.

records.name: data/ultimate/upic.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/ultimate/upic.md#Pitfalls -->
## Pitfalls

1. Upic is a technique: do not generate code expecting a mode register or a second VIC.
2. Wait out the 1 MHz window; a PRG started without its turbo `.cfg` never reaches speed (probe gives up).
3. No indexed addressing on I/O, no interrupts or DMA stalls mid-frame, no REST memory reads.
4. UCI discipline: write literal control values, bound all loops, do not send the unlock sequence if UCI already answers.
5. Compiler pitfalls with Oscar64 seen in these projects: reordered constant I/O stores (use inline asm for DMA), dropped reads of `$DC0D` (do it in asm), globals shared with the IRQ must be volatile, a data region below `$0801` moves the PRG load address.
6. `.upic` file saving needs a real UCI directory; after reset the current directory can be virtual and creation fails.
7. 240 rows instead of 256 give 31 % more free time (268,300 against 204,800 cycles).

## `0x85` - VICE Info

Gets VICE version information.

```text
cmd: empty
rsp: 0x85 | ML:u8 | MV:bytes[ML] | SL:u8 | SV:bytes[SL]
```

Example `MV = 03 05 00 00` means VICE `3.5.0.0`.

Used internally for diagnostics and backend capability checks.

---

C64 Bridge mapping:

| MCP tool    | Operation  |

Quits VICE.

```text
rsp: 0xbb | empty
```

Used internally for managed VICE lifecycle, not normally exposed as a user-facing MCP operation.

If both C64 Ultimate and VICE are configured, call `c64_select_backend` with these arguments before making VICE-specific requests:

```json
{
  "op": "select",
  "backend": "vice"
}
```

Use backend switching instead of assuming the active backend is already VICE.

## Suggested VICE Initialization

After connecting to the VICE binary monitor:

1. Send `PING`.
2. Send `VICE_INFO`.
3. Send `BANKS_AVAILABLE`.
4. Send `REGISTERS_AVAILABLE` for main memspace.
5. Cache register and bank mappings.
6. Drain or classify any asynchronous monitor events.

### Floppy Drives

| Method | Path | Parameters | Action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/v1/drives` | – | Returns information about every internal drive, including mounted images and referenced paths. |
| PUT | `/v1/drives/{drive}:mount` | `image`, `[type]`, `[mode]` | Mounts an existing image. Valid `type` values are `d64`, `g64`, `d71`, `g71`, `d81`. Valid `mode` values are `readwrite`, `readonly`, `unlinked`. |
| POST | `/v1/drives/{drive}:mount` | `[type]`, `[mode]` | Mounts an attached image. The optional arguments match the PUT variant. |
| PUT | `/v1/drives/{drive}:reset` | – | Resets the selected drive. |
| PUT | `/v1/drives/{drive}:remove` | – | Removes the mounted image from the drive. |
| PUT | `/v1/drives/{drive}:on` | – | Turns on the selected drive and resets it if already on. |
| PUT | `/v1/drives/{drive}:off` | – | Turns off the selected drive. |
| PUT | `/v1/drives/{drive}:load_rom` | `file` | Loads a 16K or 32K ROM from the Ultimate file system into the selected drive. The load is temporary. |
| POST | `/v1/drives/{drive}:load_rom` | – | Loads an attached 16K or 32K ROM into the selected drive. The load is temporary. |
| PUT | `/v1/drives/{drive}:set_mode` | `mode` | Changes the drive mode to `1541`, `1571`, or `1581`. The firmware also loads the corresponding ROM. |

Example for `/v1/drives`:

```json
{
  "drives": [
    {
      "a": {
        "enabled": true,
        "bus_id": 8,
```

## Decision Rules

- `supported`: part of the public VICE contract, enforced at runtime, documented in generated compatibility tables, and covered by regression tests.
- `mock-only experimental`: may exist in test scaffolding or backend experiments, but must not appear as supported in public MCP metadata or README compatibility tables.
- `unsupported`: blocked at runtime on VICE with `unsupported_platform`.

## Phase-One Decisions

- Resource-backed VICE drive operations are supported in phase one: `list_drives`, `mount`, `unmount`, `reset`, `power_on`, `power_off`, and `set_mode`.
- Grouped operations already declared c64u-only remain c64u-only on VICE and must be blocked at runtime.
- Mock-only behavior must not appear in public compatibility tables before it is intentionally promoted to supported status.
- For this phase, there are no public `mock-only experimental` operations in the grouped MCP contract. Any such behavior remains internal to tests or backend experiments until explicitly reclassified here.

# VICE Binary Monitor Protocol Specification

This document combines the [official documentation](https://vice-emu.sourceforge.io/vice_13.html) with research of the [monitor_binary.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/libretro/vice-libretro/refs/heads/master/vice/src/monitor/monitor_binary.c) source code for VICE 3.9 (Git ID `a072441`).

records.name: doc/vice/vice-binary-monitor-spec.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: doc/vice/vice-binary-monitor-spec.md#1. Overview -->
## 1. Overview

The Vice Binary Monitor exposes the built-in VICE monitor over a dedicated network socket (enable with `-binarymonitor`, configure the bind address with `-binarymonitoraddress` or the `BinaryMonitorServerAddress` resource).

Only one client may be connected at a time. When packets arrive the monitor traps execution (`monitor_startup_trap`), executes the requested operation, and resumes the emulated machine. The default bind target is `ip4://127.0.0.1:6502`.

All multi-byte scalar fields are encoded little endian on the wire. The monitor forwards most operations to the same helper routines used by the text monitor, so side effects, breakpoint semantics, and register layouts are identical to the CLI monitor.

---

records.name: doc/vice/vice-binary-monitor-spec.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: doc/vice/vice-binary-monitor-spec.md#Introspection (0x81–0x85) -->
### Introspection (0x81–0x85)

#### 0x81 – Ping

- Request: empty
- Response (`0x81`): empty

#### 0x82 – Banks Available

- Request: empty
- Response (`0x82`): `[0–1] count, [2+] entries` where each entry is `[size,bank_lo,bank_hi,name_len,name]`
- Notes: Data is collected from `mon_interfaces[e_comp_space]`. Each size equals `3 + name_len`.

#### 0x83 – Registers Available

- Request: `[0] memspace`
- Response (`0x83`): `[0–1] count, [2+] entries` where each entry is `[size,id,bits,name_len,name]`
- Notes: Size equals `3 + name_len`. The `bits` field is the register width reported by `mon_reg_list_t::size`. Entries flagged with `MON_REGISTER_IS_FLAGS` are skipped.

#### 0x84 – Display Get

- Request: `[0] use alternate canvas flag, [1] format (0 = indexed 8-bit)`
- Response (`0x84`): `[0–3] info length (currently 13), [4–5] debug width, [6–7] debug height, [8–9] debug X offset, [10–11] debug Y offset, [12–13] inner width, [14–15] inner height, [16] bits per pixel (8), [17–20] buffer length, [21+] pixel data`
- Notes: Requires API version `0x02`. For the C128, setting the flag selects `machine_video_canvas_get(1)` (VDC); other machines ignore the flag. The buffer contains `debug_width * debug_height` bytes. Areas outside the visible inner rectangle are zero-filled.

#### 0x85 – VICE Info

- Request: empty
- Response (`0x85`): `[0]=4, [1–4]=VERSION_RC_NUMBER, [5]=4, [6–9]=build revision (zero unless`USE_SVN_REVISION`is defined)`
- Notes: The first length covers the four RC number bytes (major, minor, build, patch).

records.name: doc/vice/vice-binary-monitor-spec.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: doc/vice/vice-binary-monitor-spec.md#Exit, Reset, Autostart (0xAA–0xDD) -->
### Exit, Reset, Autostart (0xAA–0xDD)

#### 0xAA – Exit

- Request: empty
- Response (`0xAA`): empty
- Notes: Sets `exit_mon = 1`, returning execution to the emulator while keeping VICE running.

#### 0xBB – Quit

- Request: empty
- Response (`0xBB`): empty
- Notes: Calls `mon_quit()` to terminate VICE.

#### 0xCC – Reset

- Request: `[0] reset type`
- Response (`0xCC`): empty
- Notes: Value is passed straight to `mon_reset_machine`. Common values are 0 (soft), 1 (power), 8–11 (drive resets).

#### 0xDD – Autostart

- Request: `[0] run flag (0 = load only, 1 = run), [1–2] file index, [3] file name length, [4+] path`
- Response (`0xDD`): empty
- Notes: The monitor NUL-terminates the name and calls `mon_autostart`. On success the monitor exits so the autostart can continue; failures return `0x8F`.

---

# VICE Binary Monitor vs Ultimate 64 REST API

This document compares the [VICE Binary Monitor protocol](https://vice-emu.sourceforge.io/vice_13.html) of VICE 3.9 and the [Ultimate 64 REST API](https://1541u-documentation.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/api_calls.html) using Ultimate 64 firmware 3.12a.

Each row shows how to invoke the feature through either interface and highlights functional gaps.

Legend: 🟢 green light (full support or best option), 🟡 amber light (partial or indirect support), 🔴 red light (not available here). Indicators appear at the start of each platform cell.

records.name: doc/vice/vice-bm-vs-c64u-rest.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: doc/vice/vice-bm-vs-c64u-rest.md#Machine Lifecycle -->
## Machine Lifecycle

| Capability | VICE Binary Monitor | Ultimate REST API | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Exit monitor | 🟢 `0xAA` Exit — releases control back to emulator loop. | 🟡 Not required. | REST calls run out-of-band and do not halt the CPU by default. |
| Quit emulator/device | 🟡 `0xBB` Quit — invokes `mon_quit()`. | 🟢 `PUT /v1/machine:poweroff` (powers off), `PUT /v1/machine:reboot`. | Monitor quit terminates VICE; REST poweroff stops the Ultimate hardware. |
| Reset | 🟢 `0xCC` Reset — `[reset_type]` (0 soft, 1 hard, 8–11 drive IDs). | 🟢 `PUT /v1/machine:reset` (system), `PUT /v1/drives/{drive}:reset` (per-drive). | Monitor supports fine-grained drive resets via type codes; REST splits drive resets per endpoint. |
| Pause/resume | 🟡 Resume controlled by exiting monitor; stop state signaled with `0x62/0x63`. | 🟢 `PUT /v1/machine:pause` / `PUT /v1/machine:resume`. | REST offers explicit pause control without entering a monitor. |
| Autostart/run program | 🟡 `0xDD` Autostart — `[run_flag,file_index,name_len,name_bytes]`. | 🟢 `PUT/POST /v1/runners:run_prg` (DMA load + run) or `...:load_prg` (load only). | Monitor autostart exits the monitor after queuing the autostart; REST runners reset the machine automatically. |

records.text:
<!-- Source: doc/vice/vice-bm-vs-c64u-rest.md#Snapshots, Display, and Peripherals -->
## Snapshots, Display, and Peripherals

| Capability | VICE Binary Monitor | Ultimate REST API | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Save snapshot | 🟢 `0x41` Dump Snapshot — `[save_roms,save_disks,name_len,name_bytes]`. | 🔴 Not available. | REST has no snapshot API. |
| Load snapshot | 🟢 `0x42` Undump Snapshot — `[name_len,name_bytes]`; response returns PC. | 🔴 Not available. | — |
| Display capture | 🟢 `0x84` Display Get (API `0x02`) — `[alt_canvas,mode]`; response includes geometry metadata and pixel buffer. | 🟡 `PUT /v1/streams/video:start?ip=host[:port]` for live UDP streaming (Ultimate 64 only). | Monitor provides immediate framebuffer dumps; REST streams continuous video but no single-frame capture. |
| Palette capture | 🟢 `0x91` Palette Get — `[alt_canvas]`; returns RGB triples. | 🔴 Not available. | REST lacks palette inspection. |
| Joyport output | 🟢 `0xA2` Joyport Set — `[port_lo,port_hi,value_lo,value_hi]`. | 🔴 Not available. | REST cannot toggle joystick lines. |
| Userport output | 🟢 `0xB2` Userport Set — `[value_lo,value_hi]`. | 🔴 Not available. | — |
| Keyboard injection | 🟢 `0x72` Keyboard Feed. | 🔴 Not available. | — |

<!-- Source: doc/vice/vice-bm-vs-c64u-rest.md#Configuration and Resources -->
## Configuration and Resources

| Capability | VICE Binary Monitor | Ultimate REST API | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Resource read | 🟡 `0x51` Resource Get — `[name_len,name_bytes]`; response indicates type and value. | 🟡 `GET /v1/configs`, `GET /v1/configs/{category}`, `GET /v1/configs/{category}/{item}`. | Monitor accesses emulator resource system; REST targets Ultimate firmware settings. |
| Resource write | 🟡 `0x52` Resource Set — `[type,name_len,name_bytes,value_len,value_bytes]`. | 🟡 `PUT /v1/configs/{...}?value=...`, `POST /v1/configs` (batch). | Resource namespaces differ: monitor affects VICE runtime options, REST changes Ultimate firmware configuration. |
| Batch configuration | 🔴 Not available. | 🟢 `POST /v1/configs` (nested JSON). | — |
| Load/save config to flash | 🔴 Not available. | 🟢 `PUT /v1/configs:load_from_flash`, `PUT /v1/configs:save_to_flash`. | Flash persistence is firmware-specific. |
| Factory reset config | 🔴 Not available. | 🟢 `PUT /v1/configs:reset_to_default`. | — |

records.text:
<!-- Source: doc/vice/vice-bm-vs-c64u-rest.md#Media, Drives, and Audio (REST Exclusive) -->
## Media, Drives, and Audio (REST Exclusive)

| Capability | VICE Binary Monitor | Ultimate REST API | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SID playback | 🔴 Not available. | 🟢 `PUT/POST /v1/runners:sidplay`. | Hardware audio runners are outside the scope of the monitor. |
| MOD playback | 🔴 Not available. | 🟢 `PUT/POST /v1/runners:modplay`. | — |
| Cartridge/PRG DMA load | 🟡 Autostart (`0xDD`) accepts filenames from the host FS. | 🟢 `PUT/POST /v1/runners:run_crt`, `...:run_prg`, `...:load_prg`. | Monitor runs within VICE and uses its virtual FS; REST accesses the Ultimate storage or uploaded payloads. |
| Drive management | 🔴 Not available (except checkpointing on drive CPU via memspace). | 🟢 `/v1/drives` (info), `/v1/drives/{drive}:mount`, `:remove`, `:on`, `:off`, `:set_mode`, `:load_rom`. | REST controls physical drive emulation directly. |
| File image creation | 🔴 Not available. | 🟢 `PUT /v1/files/{path}:create_d64/d71/d81/dnp`. | Monitor has no disk image authoring commands. |
| Data streams | 🔴 Not available. | 🟢 `PUT /v1/streams/<stream>:start` / `PUT /v1/streams/<stream>:stop` (stream = `video`, `audio`, `debug`). | REST can export live video/audio/debug streams. |

records.name: doc/vice/vice-bm-vs-c64u-rest.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: doc/vice/vice-bm-vs-c64u-rest.md#Observations -->
## Observations

- The VICE Binary Monitor is the only interface that exposes low-level debugger primitives (breakpoints, register manipulation, single-stepping, framebuffer snapshots, palette dumps, joystick/userport control).
- The Ultimate REST API focuses on machine orchestration and firmware-level services (DMA loading, media playback, drive management, persistent configuration, and streaming), none of which are available through the binary monitor.
- Memory access and reset operations overlap; however, the monitor supports banked address spaces and fine-grained CPU control, while the REST DMA endpoints operate on the flattened Ultimate memory view and offer coarse pause/resume semantics.
- Integrations needing both precise debugging and system management typically combine the monitor for CPU/memory inspection with REST calls for device control and file management.

# SID File Structure Reference (for RAG)

See `data/sound/sid-file-structure.md` for the complete explanation of PSID/RSID headers, fields, and playback behavior. This stub ensures the RAG index includes this topic and can surface it when generating or playing songs.

- Magic: `PSID` or `RSID`
- Key fields: version, dataOffset, loadAddress, initAddress, playAddress, songs, startSong, speed
- v2–v4 extras: flags (PAL/NTSC, 6581/8580), startPage/pageLength, second/third SID base
- Song length lookup: HVSC `Songlengths.md5` by MD5 of full file
